intended_object: The restriction of a dependent function defined on the members of the list `i :: l` to the members of `l`, i.e. the "tail" part of the decomposition f ↦ (f(i), f|_l). It is used with `List.Pi.head` and `List.Pi.cons` in the `List.pi` construction (from the docstring and module).
explanation:
The body is `fun j hj ↦ f j (mem_cons_of_mem _ hj)`, so it sends each member `j` of `l` to `f j`, using the proof that `j ∈ l` implies `j ∈ i :: l`. That is exactly the restriction of `f` to `l`, as the docstring says. The `cons_eta` lemma shows it is the right inverse partner of `cons`: `cons (head f) (tail f) = f`.

One small technicality: the `[DecidableEq ι]` section variable is probably carried into the definition even though the body never uses it. This is a harmless artifact of how the file is organised. It does not change what the function does and does not make it narrower in any meaningful way.

The definition works for an arbitrary index type `ι` and an arbitrary family `α : ι → Sort*`, so it is fully general for functions whose domain is given by list membership. Mathlib has no separate general version of this list-specific restriction (`Multiset.Pi` provides `cons` but no `tail`).
